about.title: Nevada City Slip & Fall Claims
about.longDescription: Nevada City's older buildings, wooden boardwalks, sloped sidewalks, and Gold Rush-era storefronts along Broad Street and Commercial Street create uneven walking surfaces that can catch even careful pedestrians off guard. Whether the fall happened in a downtown shop, a rental property, or a parking area near SR-49 or SR-20, California law requires the property owner to have known or reasonably should have known about the hazard before liability attaches. That's why documenting exactly what caused your fall, and pulling any nearby surveillance footage quickly, matters so much. LawProactive doesn't practice law ourselves, but we can connect you, free of charge, with an independent local attorney who understands how premises cases are built in small Sierra foothill communities. They work on contingency, meaning there's no upfront cost and no fee unless your case results in a recovery. Reaching out early gives your case the best chance of preserving the evidence it needs.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney About Your Fall

items.title: Proving the Owner Knew
items.desc: California requires showing the property owner knew or should have known about the hazard and didn't fix or warn about it. An attorney can help gather maintenance logs, prior complaints, or inspection records to establish this.

items.title: Racing Against Lost Evidence
items.desc: Surveillance footage from stores and businesses around downtown Nevada City is often overwritten within days or weeks. Acting quickly helps preserve video and witness accounts before they disappear.

items.title: Understanding Comparative Fault
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, so even if you're found partly responsible for the fall, you may still recover a reduced amount. An attorney can help present your side clearly if the property owner tries to shift blame.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in Nevada City?
items.answer: Generally, California gives you two years from the date of the fall to file a premises liability claim. If the property involved is owned by a public entity, such as a city or county building, the deadline is much shorter and requires an earlier claim notice. Because these timelines vary, it's best to speak with an attorney as soon as possible.

items.question: What if I fell on uneven sidewalk pavement near a downtown business?
items.answer: Sidewalk conditions in older commercial areas like Nevada City's historic district can raise questions about which party, the adjacent business or the local government, is responsible for maintenance. This often depends on easement agreements and municipal code. An independent attorney can help sort out who may be liable in your specific situation.

items.question: Will I owe money upfront to get help with my claim?
items.answer: No. LawProactive's connection service is free, and attorneys in the network typically work on contingency, meaning they only get paid if your case results in a recovery. There's no obligation to move forward after speaking with an attorney.
